import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper using Python's html.unescape for standard cases
import html

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str,expected",
    [
        # Basic entities
        ("&", "&"),
        ("<", "<"),
        (">", ">"),
        (""", '"'),
        ("'", "'"),
        # Multiple entities
        ("A & B < C > D", "A & B < C > D"),
        # No entities
        ("Hello world!", "Hello world!"),
        # Empty string
        ("", ""),
        # None input
        (None, None),
        # Incomplete entity should stay unchanged
        ("Hello &", "Hello &"),
        ("Hello &amp", "Hello &amp"),
        ("Hello &; world", "Hello &; world"),
        # Entity with extra ampersand (old regex should NOT replace)
        ("&&", "&&"),
        # Entity with ampersand inside name (unlikely but test old behavior)
        ("&a&b;", "&a&b;"),
        # Mixed text with stray semicolons
        ("Test ; & ; end", "Test ; & ; end"),
        # Entity at start and end
        ("&Start and end>", "&Start and end>"),
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_basic(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_consistency_with_html_unescape():
    """Compare behavior on a range of typical HTML strings where html.unescape is reliable."""
    samples = [
        "The price is £100 & tax.",
        "5 < 10 && 10 > 5",
        "Use "quotes" and 'apostrophes'.",
        "Unicode: ☃ ☃",
        "Mixed: & < &unknown; &",
    ]
    for s in samples:
        # html.unescape leaves unknown entities unchanged, which matches old behavior
        assert unescapeHTML(s) == html.unescape(s)


def test_unescapeHTML_edge_cases():
    # Very long string with many entities
    long_str = ("&" * 1000) + "end"
    expected = ("&" * 1000) + "end"
    assert unescapeHTML(long_str) == expected

    # String with consecutive ampersands that should not be collapsed
    s = "&&&&&"
    # Old behavior: only the isolated & should be unescaped, others stay
    # The pattern matches the & after the third '&'
    # Result: "&&&&&&"
    # However, because the old regex disallows '&' inside the entity, it will match only the last &
    # So expected result:
    expected = "&&&&&&"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected

    # Zero-length entity (invalid) should stay unchanged
    assert unescapeHTML("&;") == "&;"

    # Entity with only semicolon after ampersand
    assert unescapeHTML("&;test") == "&;test"
